stem: What is a "golden set" in LLM application testing?

options.text: A set of the most expensive prompts
A curated set of inputs with expected outputs or acceptance criteria used to detect regressions when prompts, models or data change
The first thousand users
A vendor benchmark

explanation: A golden set is a stable, representative regression suite. Run it before changing a prompt, model, retrieval setup or data.

stem: Which metric tells you whether the relevant passage appears among the top k retrieved results?

options.text: Perplexity
Recall at k
Latency
Token count

explanation: Recall@k measures whether relevant items are retrieved within the top k. It evaluates retrieval separately from generation.

stem: Using a language model to judge another model's outputs ("LLM-as-judge") is best treated as:

options.text: A ground truth that needs no checking
A scalable but biased signal that should be calibrated against human labels and combined with deterministic checks
Illegal
Only useful for translation

explanation: Judge models are useful at scale but can be biased (for example towards length or their own style). Calibrate them against human judgement and complement with objective checks.

stem: A team swaps its model for a cheaper one and tests by trying ten prompts by hand. Two weeks later users report worse answers on refund questions.

options.text: Build a representative evaluation set from real, anonymised questions (including refund cases), define pass criteria, and run it automatically before any model or prompt change, with a rollout that can be reverted.
Keep manual spot-checks but try twenty prompts instead of ten.
Ask users to report problems and fix them as they arise.
Revert to the expensive model permanently.

rationales.text: Representative data and criteria make quality changes measurable.
Spot checks give statistically reliable coverage of rare high-impact cases.
Automation lets every change be tested cheaply and repeatedly.
User reports are an adequate test strategy for high-impact domains.

explanation: Without a representative evaluation set, regressions in important categories go unnoticed. Automate the evaluation and tie changes to it.
model_answer: Sample and anonymise real queries, label or define criteria per category, automate the run in CI, gate changes on thresholds, and monitor after release with rollback available.

rubric.criterion: Representative evaluation set including high-impact cases

stem: A RAG assistant gives wrong answers. Product owners blame the model; engineers suspect retrieval. You can log retrieved passages and generated answers.
constraints: Need to find the failing component quickly
Labelled question and passage pairs exist for 150 queries
Generation and retrieval are separate components

options.text: Evaluate retrieval and generation separately: measure recall at k on the labelled pairs, then judge answers given the correct passages, to localise whether retrieval or generation fails.
Swap the model and see if answers improve.
Rewrite the prompt several times.
Collect more user feedback before doing anything.

rationales.text: End-to-end accuracy alone shows where the fault is.
Providing the gold passage to the generator isolates generation quality.
Prompt rewriting is the quickest way to find a retrieval fault.

explanation: Separating retrieval metrics from generation quality identifies the failing stage, avoiding costly guesswork.
model_answer: Compute recall and ranking metrics on labelled pairs, run the generator with gold passages to test its faithfulness, compare results, then fix the weaker component.
